meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('buongiorno') used directly in spoken exchanges.

examples.text: Бонжорно, синьоры, добро пожаловать к нам!
examples.trans: Buongiorno, signori, welcome to our place!

examples.text: Шеф весело сказал всем гостям бонжорно.
examples.trans: The chef cheerfully said buongiorno to all the guests.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'иньора'). Common feminine noun meaning 'signora' in everyday Russian.
Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'kind', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'позвать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
как тебя зовут? = what's your name? меня зовут ... = my name is ...
Everyday conversational Russian name meaning 'Alexander', frequent in spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ставка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'exhibition' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A representative of the exhibition from Milan called.

examples.text: Почему, Вик, на выставку не улетели?
examples.trans: Why didn't you fly out to the exhibition?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'меняться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be canceled', forming an aspectual pair with 'отмениться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: С этого момента вся правда отменяется!
examples.trans: From this moment on, all truth is canceled!

передать.gloss: to pass on, to hand over

meanings.en: to pass on, to hand over, to give
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'дать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to pass on', forming an aspectual pair with 'передавать'.

examples.trans: Please pass on my regards to your mum.

examples.text: Всё, я ухожу. Ребёнок ни при чём. Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: That's it, I'm leaving. The child isn't to blame. Give this to Alexei.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('grazie') used directly in spoken exchanges.

examples.text: Граци, синьора, ваш столик у окна уже полностью готов!
examples.trans: Grazie, signora, your table by the window is already completely ready!

examples.text: Итальянский гость с улыбкой сказал официанту граци за отличный кофе.
examples.trans: With a smile the Italian guest said grazie to the waiter for the excellent coffee.

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('ciao-ciao') used directly in spoken exchanges.

examples.text: Граци, синьора, чао-чао, ждём вас снова завтра вечером!
examples.trans: Grazie, signora, ciao-ciao, we look forward to seeing you again tomorrow evening!

examples.text: Луи весело помахал всем рукой и крикнул чао-чао.
examples.trans: Louis cheerfully waved his hand to everyone and called out ciao-ciao.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
only when answering or making a phone call

examples.text: Алло, Вика, ты сейчас где находишься?
examples.trans: Hello, Vika, where are you right now?

meanings.note: polite, or to several people; the first в is silent

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'позвонить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to ring') (a bell or phone) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ставитель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'representative' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A representative of the exhibition from Milan called.

examples.text: Сегодня утром звонил официальный представитель выставки из Милана.
examples.trans: An official representative of the exhibition from Milan called this morning.

examples.text: В зале сидит представитель крупной французской винодельни.
examples.trans: A representative of a major French winery is sitting in the dining room.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian name meaning 'Milana', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A representative of the exhibition from Milan called.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'модедово').

examples.text: А, правда? Я уже в Домодедово.
examples.trans: Oh, really? I am already in Domodedovo.

examples.text: Я уже еду в аэропорт Домодедово встречать гостей.
examples.trans: I am already driving to Domodedovo Airport to meet the guests.

examples.text: Самолёт из Парижа прилетает в Домодедово ровно в пять.
examples.trans: The plane from Paris lands at Domodedovo at five sharp.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'a little'.
чуть не + verb: я чуть не упал = I nearly fell

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

улететь.gloss: to fly away, to depart by plane

meanings.en: to fly away, to fly out, to depart by air
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'лететь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fly away', forming an aspectual pair with 'улетать'.

examples.trans: What do you mean you didn't fly out?
Our plane has already flown out.

examples.text: Да, Аллочка? Как ты не улетела? Почему?
examples.trans: Yes, Allochka? What do you mean you didn't fly out? Why?

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упредить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to warn', forming an aspectual pair with 'предупреждать'.

examples.trans: And they warned me very strictly!
